clue.text: Cut corners for a start, and jumped

indicators.note: for a start asks for just the opening letter of the word beside it

parts.note: someone who jumped on one leg hopped

explanation.surface: Someone took a shortcut to begin with and then leapt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut corners' is a set phrase, but it splits: 'Cut' alone is the definition and 'for a start' takes only the first letter of 'corners'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: wood or vegetables that have been hacked into pieces with a blade.

clue.text: Appeals for weapons to be given to church

indicators.note: the weapons are handed to the church, so they are attached to it

parts.note: arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Pleas go out for guns to be handed over to the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeals' reads as pleas, but here it means attractive qualities; 'to be given to' attaches the weapons to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of attractions: a person's appeals are their allurements.

clue.text: Production that is offset

parts.note: the first half, off, means out (the lights are off, the lights are out)
the second half, set, means put (set it down, put it down)

explanation.surface: Manufacturing whose cost is balanced by something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offset' must be split into off and set, each replaced by a synonym; the setter gives no signal for the split beyond 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the quantity a factory makes is its yield.

clue.text: Old papers mother and father found about church millions

indicators.note: the mother and father are found around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a mother and father are parents

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad discover ancient documents concerning a church's fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found about' puts CHM (church plus millions) inside PARENTS; 'about' is not 'concerning' here.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: documents written on animal skin are ancient manuscripts.

clue.text: Unusual credo of interior design

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the next word are not in their normal order

explanation.surface: A decorator has a strange set of beliefs about doing up rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges the letters of 'credo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the furnishing and colour scheme of a room.

clue.text: Flourish, but see deprivation amidst returning rabble

indicators.note: amidst places the deprivation in the middle of the rabble
returning means the word for rabble comes back, read right to left

parts.note: a rabble is a mob
a deprivation is a loss

explanation.surface: Things thrive, yet poverty is visible among the crowd coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives BOM, the rabble read backwards, and 'amidst' places the deprivation within it; 'but see' merely joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to thrive or bloom.

clue.text: Negotiated with lawyers — and won!

parts.note: barristers collectively are the Bar
won means gained, as in won ground

explanation.surface: Someone haggled alongside their legal team and came out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: haggled over terms.

clue.text: Love to crew for country

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, written O
to crew a ship is to man it

explanation.surface: Someone adores sailing as part of a team for their nation.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Confinement of a sort for royalist!

indicators.note: of a sort suggests the following letters are sorted into another order

explanation.surface: A supporter of the king is locked up after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a sort' rearranges the letters of 'royalist'; the surface suggests it merely qualifies the confinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for the prison punishment of being kept alone in a cell.

clue.text: Slow to get up — almost time, but what time?

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: slow-witted means dim
nigh means almost, as in nigh on impossible
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A late riser is asked whether they know how late it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns DIM into MID; 'almost time' is two pieces, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: twelve o'clock in the dark hours answers the question.

clue.text: Bill hill is one to take on roles

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A man called Bill Hill is someone who plays parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a stage or film performer plays parts.

clue.text: Clipped dog got temperature and suffered

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
one who suffered from illness ailed

explanation.surface: A freshly trimmed pet came down with a fever and was poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: cut short.

clue.text: Groan unhappily after opening bars played by one

definitions.note: the definition is 'one', an instrument, described as something bars of music are played by

indicators.note: after says the jumbled word follows the opening in the answer

parts.note: a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

indicators.note: unhappily says the word before it is upset, its letters disturbed

explanation.surface: A listener moans miserably once someone has performed the first few bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges 'Groan' and 'after' places the result behind the opening. The definition is back to front: the instrument is the 'one' that bars of music are played by, not opening bars of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is an instrument on which bars of music get blown.

clue.text: Beat music regularly provides such a case

indicators.note: regularly takes letters at even intervals from the two words before it

explanation.surface: Sixties pop reliably supplies an example of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every second letter of 'Beat music', starting with the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental holder for needles and such, a crossword staple.

clue.text: CIA pet name for setting free

indicators.note: for setting says these letters are to be set, arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The spy agency has a nickname for releasing a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for setting' rearranges CIA PET NAME; 'setting free' looks like one phrase, but only 'free', as a verb, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to liberate from bondage.

clue.text: Notes from demonstration by union?

indicators.note: by sets the demonstration beside the union, following it

parts.note: a wedding is a union of two people
a protest march is a demonstration

explanation.surface: Memos sent out about a protest organised by a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets the demonstration beside the union. The surface suggests a trade union protest and written memos; the union is a marriage and the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Music played as the bride walks: a tune is a sequence of sounds.

clue.text: Groom, at home, goes outside for bandages

parts.note: to groom a horse is to dress it
in means at home

indicators.note: outside takes just the outer letters of the word before it

explanation.surface: The bridegroom, who was indoors, pops out to fetch some first-aid supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes the first and last letters of 'goes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: coverings applied to wounds.

clue.text: Salary rumoured to support idiot provides relief

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the idiot

parts.note: an ass is an idiot

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard, so the word for salary is heard and not written

parts.note: a salary is wages

explanation.surface: The pay supposedly given to keep a fool going eases things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rumoured' makes WAGES heard as the ending -UAGES, and 'to support' puts it beneath ASS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym phrase: soothes or eases pain.

clue.text: Number 1 metal soldier got up firing

indicators.note: in a down clue, got up means the whole run of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the figure 1 looks like the letter I
tin is a metal
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: The top toy soldier stood up while the guns were shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' turns NO I TIN GI, read as one run, upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting of combustion in an engine is its sparking.

clue.text: Hardest gig in rock, playing like this!

definitions.note: the definition asks for a way of playing, a noun phrase

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the three words before it are shaken up

explanation.surface: The toughest concert a band could do is one performed this way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' is an instruction to shake up HARDEST GIG IN, not a kind of music; 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing music from a score never seen before is one way of performing.

clue.text: Red followed by green — making progress of a sort!

definitions.note: used as an adjective: progress in fits and starts

indicators.note: followed by gives the order: the red piece first, then the green

parts.note: a red traffic light means stop
a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: Traffic lights change and the cars move on, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes movement or policy that proceeds in fits and starts, haltingly.

clue.text: People say you can help everyone to start getting soul

indicators.note: to start takes the starting letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: Folk claim you are able to assist all in beginning to find spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes the first letters of the six words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the Greek word for the spirit or mind.

clue.text: Fool following university module

indicators.note: following puts the fool after the university

parts.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: An idiot is taking a college course component.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: one self-contained part of a course.

clue.text: Thus, spies occupy seats designed for companions

indicators.note: occupy says the first two pieces take up room within the rearranged word
designed says the word before it is fashioned into a new shape

parts.note: so means thus
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: So secret agents sit in chairs made for their partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' turns SEATS into ASTES, and 'occupy' puts SOCIA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: colleagues or partners one keeps company with.

clue.text: Ring exercises — oddly real drama

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the letter O
PE, physical education, is exercises at school

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word after it

explanation.surface: Gymnastics on the rings turn out to be strangely genuine theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first and third letters of 'real'. Wagner's Ring makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sung stage work is a kind of theatre.

clue.text: Love to see a student chasing victory at this ground

indicators.note: chasing puts the last two pieces behind the victory

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, written O
V stands for victory, as in V-sign
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A fan enjoys watching a pupil pursue a win at this sports venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts A and L after V. The Oval is a London cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a famous London cricket venue, usually named with 'the'.

clue.text: Vegan rice freaks get gripe

indicators.note: freaks, as a verb, means goes wild, so the two words before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: People obsessed with plant-based grain dishes have a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freaks' is a verb here, rearranging VEGAN RICE, not a noun for fanatics.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a complaint.

clue.text: A short film about walrus' tail in jelly

indicators.note: about wraps the first three words around the tail letter

parts.note: pic is a shortened word for a film, a picture

indicators.note: tail takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A brief documentary on the rear end of a walrus set in gelatine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps A PIC around S, the 'tail' of walrus.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a savoury clear setting made from meat stock.

clue.text: Form of tennis the French put on grass

indicators.note: put on adds the French word to the end of the other piece

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing to the police, as is to sing
les is 'the' in French, in the plural

explanation.surface: A version of the game that France stages on lawn courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' adds LES to SING. 'grass' is not the court surface: it is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: matches played one against one.

clue.text: Growth restricted by insane moneylenders

indicators.note: restricted by says the answer is held within the limits of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Economic expansion is held back by crazy loan sharks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' confines the answer within 'insane moneylenders'; the growth is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a flowering plant is something that grows.
